Tritium (³H) is radioactive. - **Low Density**: At STP, H₂ is 11.2 times lighter than air, making it highly buoyant. - **High Diffusivity**: Hydrogen diffuses through solids and liquids faster than any other gas. - **Flammability Limits**: 4–75 % (v/v) in air; can form explosive mixtures with oxygen or air. - **Energy Content**: Combustion of 1 kg of H₂ releases ~120 MJ, comparable to gasoline (~44 MJ kg⁻¹). - **Electrochemical Use**: Hydrogen is a key reactant in fuel cells (producing electricity and water). - **Spectroscopy**: The Lyman series (UV) and Balmer series (visible) are classic hydrogen spectral lines. --- ### How Hydrogen Is Used in Practice | Application | Why Hydrogen? | Typical Conditions | |-------------|---------------|--------------------| | **Fuel Cells** | Clean energy carrier; it emits β‑radiation; use shielding and monitoring. --- ### Further Reading - *Physical Chemistry* by Peter Atkins & Julio de Paula – Chapter on gases and thermodynamics. - *Introduction to Quantum Mechanics* by David J. Griffiths – Section on hydrogen atom energy levels. - *Hydrogen: A Renewable Energy Source* – International Energy Agency reports. - *NIST Chemistry WebBook* – Detailed thermodynamic data for hydrogen and its compounds.
